messages:
IncidentBot: INCIDENT detected (sev1 candidate) — spike of 502/503 responses from Okta auth endpoints in us-east-1, multiple customers reporting console login failures and token verification errors. Auto-page sent to oncall. Logs show >60% failure rate for /introspect and /oauth2/v1/token in last 5m.
Maya (oncall-sre): paging in. seeing it in our dashboards — auth failure rate from okta-prod up 12x. can someone grab the runbook? @chen @diego
Chen (platform): on it. runbook: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/auth-provider-failure — starting checklist. first step: confirm scope (customers vs internal admin), second: try cached-lookup fallback.
Rina (support): we've got 23 open CS tickets in last 10m. sample: customer_id=acme-42 "unable to sign in, returns 503". multiple enterprise customers reporting console lockouts.
Diego (eng-runtime): pasting reproducer logs from one of our services (redwood-auth-proxy):
```
2026-03-15T18:02:11.342Z ERROR okta_introspect request failed status=503 body="Service Unavailable"
2026-03-15T18:02:11.343Z WARN jwt_verification error="issuer_unreachable" tenant=acme-42 token_id=xxxtoken
2026-03-15T18:02:12.001Z ERROR user_login failed user_id=alice reason="introspect: 503"
```
curl to Okta endpoint returns 503/502 intermittently:
```
$ curl -v https://okta-us.example.com/oauth2/v1/introspect -d 'token=xxx'
> HTTP/1.1 503 Service Temporarily Unavailable\n< Service Unavailable\n```
Diego (eng-runtime): initial hypothesis: regional Okta gateway issue or upstream cert rotation causing load balancers to respond 502/503. Not seeing auth header signature mismatches — more upstream service errors.
Maya (oncall-sre): severity check: this is affecting sign-ins and console access across customers => declare SEV1. Notifying exec and opening incident bridge.
IncidentBot: Bridge opened: https://zoom.internal/bridge/incident-1765234567 (host: maya). Pager duty escalation path followed.
Chen (platform): temporary mitigations we can try now: 1) enable local token cache fallback for previously-verified sessions (TTL++), 2) disable strict introspect fallback enforcement for console routes so long-lived session cookies can be accepted, 3) create emergency admin bypass for support (short-lived service token). I'll prepare config flips.
Maya (oncall-sre): Chen — run the cache toggle, post commands and changes here. Diego — monitor error rate and token rejection counters. Rina — prep customer comms. Sam — quick risk check for bypass.
Chen (platform): executing feature-flag flip:
```
# enable cached fallback for console sessions
curl -XPOST https://flags.internal/api/flags/auth:console_cached_fallback -d '{"value":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'
# result: 200 OK
```
Chen (platform): also bumped local cache TTL from 5m -> 20m for token cache on auth-proxy. Pushed config via deploy pipeline.
Sam (security): emergency bypass needs strict guardrails. if we create admin bypass, rotate creds, MFA required, audit logging to S3, and a kill-switch. Approve only for support engineers. Rina please list which support users need access.
Rina (support): listing: @ash, @tori, @mike. will require 2FA and ephemeral tokens. drafting customer-facing line: "We're experiencing an authentication provider outage affecting sign-ins and console access in us-east-1. Engineers are investigating; a temporary mitigation is being rolled out to restore sessions. We will update in 30 minutes." Thoughts?
Maya (oncall-sre): good. post to status page and paste draft to incident status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1765234567 — update: posted.
Okta Support Bot: Okta case #OKTA-789102 opened. Okta acknowledges service degradation in us-east-1 — investigating internal gateway and cert rotation. ETA unknown. We'll update within 15m.
Diego (eng-runtime): metrics update: auth failures dropped from 62% -> 28% after cache TTL bump and cached-fallback flip. Console login success for previously-active sessions improved, but fresh sign-ins still failing.
Maya (oncall-sre): good. keep monitoring. Rina — push interim note to impacted customers via support tickets: mention workaround (relogin may fail; we are restoring existing sessions).
Rina (support): sent batch reply to top-10 impacted: "We're applying temporary session-fallback to reduce impact; you may need to refresh the console — support can create short-lived admin sessions if required."
Chen (platform): next mitigation attempt (if Okta doesn't recover): route introspect to secondary region or fallback auth provider for non-SAML tenants. preparing canary switch: config snippet:
```
# route introspect to fallback region
curl -XPOST https://config.internal/api/routes/auth -d '{"introspect_preference":["okta-us-east","okta-us-west"]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'
```
Maya (oncall-sre): wait for Okta update. if they don't respond in 15m, we'll canary the region switch for low-traffic tenants only. Diego please prepare rollback plan.
Okta Support Bot: Update: We have identified a misconfigured gateway causing 503s for some tenants in us-east-1; mitigation in progress. We'll follow up with post-mortem.
Diego (eng-runtime): added health-checks and increased quick-retry for introspect calls to smooth transient errors. code pushed to staging.
Maya (oncall-sre): handoff note for next oncall (Chen) at 19:00 UTC:
- SEV1 ongoing — Okta us-east-1 degradation.
- Mitigations applied: cache TTL bumped, console_cached_fallback enabled, emergency admin bypass prepared (not yet granted).
- Impact: ~28% auth failure as of last check; primary impact is fresh sign-ins and console login for new sessions. Several enterprise customers on older SSO configs affected.
- Next actions: monitor Okta updates, prepare region-canary switch for introspect if no Okta recovery in 15-30m, coordinate customer comms with Rina, be ready to provide emergency admin sessions if approved by Sam.
Chen (platform): I acknowledge handoff. will take 1st watch and continue checks. will escalate to org if error rate creeps above 50% again.
Sam (security): reaffirming: admin bypass only with 2 approvals (one from SRE lead + security). All sessions must be audited.
Maya (oncall-sre): thanks team — handing off to @chen. will remain on-call for exec briefing.
IncidentBot: reminder: attach post-incident notes and tag the incident with labels: [okta, third_party, sev1, auth-failure].
Rina (support): customer impact summary to paste in postmortem: "~15 enterprise customers experienced console lockouts; approx 3% of total active sessions were disrupted; affected customers mostly in us-east region. Temporary mitigations restored existing sessions; fresh sign-ins partially degraded until Okta remediation."
Okta Support Bot: Update: Okta mitigation completed in us-east-1, monitoring. We will provide a root cause timeline in 24h. Case OKTA-789102.
Maya (oncall-sre): monitoring shows auth failure rate back to baseline (<1%). declaring incident resolved from our side. will keep incident open for postmortem collection.
Rina (support): closing customer comms loop. drafting post-incident email for impacted customers.
Chen (platform): collecting logs and metrics for postmortem. linking runbook and actions to the incident doc.
Maya (oncall-sre): closing bridge. final note: follow-up postmortem to include why cached-fallback wasn't enabled by default, and whether we need automatic region failover for introspect.
